evals.name: general-package-stow
evals.prompt: I installed a local CLI under ~/opt/stow/mytool with bin/mytool and share/man/man1/mytool.1. Help me stow it into ~/opt without touching anything unexpected.
evals.expected_output: A safe GNU Stow workflow using explicit stow and target directories, a dry-run before mutation, and verification of resulting relative symlinks.
assertions: Identifies the stow directory, target directory, package name, and action
Runs or recommends stow with -n before the mutating command
Uses explicit -d and -t options rather than relying only on cwd defaults
Explains that Stow creates target symlinks and does not delete the package directory
Includes a verification step for created symlinks

evals.name: restow-after-update
evals.prompt: I removed a file from /usr/local/stow/foo/bin and added a new one. What's the right way to refresh the links in /usr/local?
evals.expected_output: Guidance to use restow with dry-run first, explaining that restow unstows obsolete links and stows current package contents.
assertions: Recommends stow -R for refreshing package links
Runs or recommends a dry-run restow before applying
States that restow removes obsolete owned symlinks but not package files
Uses /usr/local/stow as stow directory and /usr/local as target when matching the prompt

evals.name: conflict-boundary
evals.prompt: stow says it can't stow package foo because /usr/local/bin/foo already exists. Help me fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent should switch from normal package management to conflict triage and avoid overwriting the existing target file.
assertions: Recognizes this as a conflict-resolution task rather than a clean stow workflow
Does not recommend deleting or overwriting the existing file without approval
Checks whether the existing path is owned by Stow
Mentions using the debug-stow-conflicts workflow or equivalent triage
